Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the basted fitting — the first try-on stage of a bespoke suit, with the canvas hand-tacked in white thread. Counter to using a famous surname (Henry Poole is an active TM in tailoring). Basted names the process, not a heritage firm.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern bespoke is shifting from heritage signaling toward process literacy. Customers want to know what stage they're in, what's being hand-stitched, and what the second fitting will fix.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Saman Amel (samanamel.com) plays the modern atelier peer. Drake's (drakes.com) holds the considered-tailoring middle. Anderson & Sheppard (anderson-sheppard.co.uk) is the Savile Row reference. We sit as a process-named modern bespoke house.
Modern.positioningStatement: Basted & Co. is a modern bespoke tailor that names its trade by the basted fitting, not by a heritage surname.

targetAudience.primary: Men 30-50 commissioning their first or second bespoke suit and reading about half canvas before they book.
behaviors: Ask about canvas and shoulder build
Return for a second commission within 24 months

dos: Name the fitting stage on every appointment confirmation
List what's hand-stitched and what's machined
Show the basted garment, white thread visible
donts: Lean on borrowed Savile Row mythology
Photograph the cutter in soft focus

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: BASTED & CO. set in a precise grotesk, all caps, ampersand drawn slightly heavier. Small mark: a single basted seam, three white tacking stitches on a navy ground, used on the inside ticket pocket.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for measurements and fitting notes
typography.rationale: One grotesk family plus its mono — the fitting-card register.

Luxury.tagline: A house on the street behind the Row.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Conduit Street, which runs one block north of Savile Row and houses several of the great bespoke firms (Huntsman's old courtyard, the Henry Poole archive). Counter to Henry Poole & Co. (active TM) and to any direct Savile Row claim. Conduit places the brand in the right square mile without copying a protected name.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury bespoke remains a small institutional category — twelve to fifteen houses in London, a similar number in Naples, each measured on cutter pedigree and clientele continuity.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Huntsman (huntsmansavilerow.com) plays the heritage-Row peer. Anderson & Sheppard (anderson-sheppard.co.uk) holds the drape-cut reference. Rubinacci (marianorubinacci.net) is the Neapolitan reference. We sit as a quieter Conduit Street house in the same register.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Conduit Bespoke is a London bespoke tailoring house operating one block off Savile Row in the Conduit Street tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Long-standing bespoke clients commissioning two to four suits a year, often through a family relationship with the cutter.
behaviors: Commission across multiple cutters in the same house
Refer family members by introduction only

dos: Name the cutter and the coatmaker
Send a hand-signed letter with each commission

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: CONDUIT BESPOKE set in a refined English serif, two lines centered, with a small house-number flourish. A hallmark — a single scissor silhouette — used on the order book and the cutter's calling card.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and the order book
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for client letters
typography.rationale: Two classical English serifs — the Conduit Street letter register.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: tailor's chalk — the cutter's first mark on the cloth. Counter to Cut (too generic) and Seam. (punctuation-led, harder to register). Chalk is the specific trade noun, single syllable.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal tailoring brands serve the design-literate professional buying their first considered suit. The opening is for a single-syllable trade-noun house with no surname, no Row claim, no story.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Saman Amel (samanamel.com) plays the modern-minimal peer. The Anthology (theanthology.cc) holds the considered-modern middle. Drake's (drakes.com) is the broader reference. We sit as the single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Chalk is a minimal bespoke tailor — one cutter, one fit, one rate card.

targetAudience.primary: Professionals 28-45 commissioning their first considered suit and wanting the appointment over with in two fittings.

dos: Publish the rate card on the home page
Show the cloth, not the lifestyle
Confirm the fitting in one line
donts: Use the word bespoke as marketing

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: CHALK set very large in a clean modern sans, five letters, one word. No symbol. The chalk mark itself — a single curved line — used as the secondary mark on the inside label.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-trade register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Cavendish Square — a real London square adjacent to the bespoke trade quarter, and a long-running British surname used by institutional firms. Counter to Henry Poole & Co. (active TM). Cavendish reads as an established trade-house name without conflict.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate bespoke and made-to-measure operates at the intersection of trunk shows, multi-city showrooms, and uniform programs for finance and law firms. The buyer is a partner, a HR director, or a head of corporate gifting.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Ede & Ravenscroft (edeandravenscroft.com) plays the institutional-uniform peer. Gieves & Hawkes (gievesandhawkes.com) holds the corporate-heritage middle. Brioni (brioni.com) is the international corporate reference. We sit as a multi-city corporate tailoring firm in the Cavendish register.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Cavendish Tailoring Co. provides bespoke and made-to-measure tailoring to professional firms, multi-city showrooms, and corporate gifting programs.

targetAudience.primary: Managing partners, HR directors, and heads of corporate gifting at finance, law, and consulting firms.

dos: Lead with the firm program, not the single suit
Speak to partners and HR directors

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: CAVENDISH TAILORING CO. set in an institutional serif, three lines centered. A small house mark — a stylized square with a single rule beneath — used on the contract cover.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the institutional tailoring register.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the thimble and the thread — the smallest and oldest tools on the cutter's bench, used together by every hand-stitcher in the trade. Counter to overplayed creative names (The Basted Fox felt costume-y; Cut, Pinned, Pressed reads as a tagline, not a brand). Thimble & Thread is the artisan pairing that lives on signage and a label tag.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative bespoke brands sit between alterations and full bespoke, often run by a single tailor-owner with a strong artisan identity. The opening is for a brand that names the tools rather than the trade.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Drake's (drakes.com) plays the artisan-modern peer. The Anthology (theanthology.cc) holds the considered-creative middle. Husbands Paris (husbands-paris.com) is the cutter-led reference. We sit as a tools-named creative tailoring house.
Creative.positioningStatement: Thimble & Thread is a creative bespoke tailor named for the two oldest tools on the cutter's bench.

targetAudience.primary: Design-aware professionals 28-45 commissioning a first suit or jacket with a story they can tell.
behaviors: Return for a second commission within 18 months

dos: Name the tailor on the inside label
Show the thimble and the thread, plainly
Write the appointment confirmation in the tailor's voice
donts: Photograph the workshop in soft focus

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: THIMBLE & THREAD set in a warm display serif with a hand-drawn ampersand. A small mark — a single thimble with one looped thread — used as the inside-label stamp.

typography.rationale: A warm display serif plus a clean grotesk — the artisan tailoring register.
